title: claim resolves the operator and asks coord inside the claims-ledger lock, so a slow claude or a slow served coord holds the lock that dispatch and other claims wait on past its stale age
goal: claim resolves the operator before it takes the claims-ledger lock; claim makes no coord call inside the lock that can outlast the lock's stale age, so a slow coord or claude never lets a waiting claim clear a live lock

run:
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import backlog, bl_base, bl_items
r = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(r), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
g("init", "-q")
(r / "backlog.json").write_text(json.dumps({"item_dir": "items"}))
(r / "items").mkdir()
item = {"id": "ST-aaaaaaaa", "kind": "story", "title": "t", "status": "todo", "priority": "P3", "goal": "g",
        "touches": ["x.txt"], "checks": [{"run": ["python3", "-c", "pass"]}]}
(r / "items" / "ST-aaaaaaaa.json").write_text(json.dumps(item, indent=2) + "\n")
g("add", "-A")
g("-c", "user.name=x", "-c", "user.email=x@example.com", "commit", "-qm", "i")
lock = bl_items.claims_ledger(r)[1].with_name(bl_items.claims_ledger(r)[1].name + ".lock")
held = {"operator": 0, "slow": []}
who = bl_items.operator_who
def spy_who(*a, **k):
    held["operator"] += lock.exists()
    return who(*a, **k)
bl_items.operator_who = spy_who
run = subprocess.run
def spy_run(*a, **k):
    if lock.exists() and (k.get("timeout") or 0) >= bl_base.LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_S:
        held["slow"].append(k["timeout"])
    return run(*a, **k)
subprocess.run = spy_run
os.environ["CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"] = "chk"
os.environ.pop("KB_BACKLOG_CONFIG", None)
code = backlog.main(["--root", str(r), "claim", "ST-aaaaaaaa", "--by", "w"])
print("claim exit", code, "| operator resolved under the ledger lock:", held["operator"],
      "| coord calls under it that can outlast its stale age:", held["slow"])
sys.exit(0 if code == 0 and not held["operator"] and not held["slow"] else 1)

claim makes no coord call inside the lock that can outlast the lock's stale age, so a slow coord or claude never lets a waiting claim clear a live lock

gates.question: How does claim keep its operator lookup and coord call from outlasting the claims-ledger lock's stale age?
options: Move both before the lock and put the run state back to released when a refusal under the lock follows
Keep take_claim under the lock and bound the coord call below the stale age
gates.recommendation: Move both before the lock and put the run state back to released when a refusal under the lock follows
gates.reason: a bound below 60 s would cut a slow but healthy coord short, and the claude and git calls in operator_who have no bound under it either
gates.answer: Move both before the lock and put the run state back to released when a refusal under the lock follows

notes: Review G3: bl_items.py:376 calls take_claim inside ledger_lock; COORD_SECONDS 60 (bl_clean.py:104) equals LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_S 60 (bl_base.py:693). The repro reads the bound only; moving the call out of the lock also fixes it. Merged with ST-v2emks5y (dropped): cmd_claim calls operator_who() (claude auth status and git config, 5 s each) after take_claim, both inside ledger_lock; BG-qggrwb5c's review gap G3: bl_items.py cmd_claim calls take_claim inside ledger_lock and COORD_SECONDS 60 (bl_clean.py) equals LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_S 60 (bl_base.py). Premise run 2026-11-09 on the base: the repro runs a claim on a planted repo with spies and prints operator resolved under the ledger lock: 1, coord calls under it that can outlast its stale age: [60]. The fix is the worker's choice (take the run state outside the lock, or bound the coord call below the stale age); a claim keeps its refusals (a held run state, the busy session) and its race rule: the same key and a different key (ST-j2eeme66), so a planted second claim of the same item still loses.
